content_units: Best Laptop Fit for a Statistics Graduate Student

Your priorities point strongly toward a machine that is easy to carry all day, lasts through classes and coding sessions, and stays comfortable for reading papers. Based on those priorities,   A is the best overall choice  , with   D   as the best value alternative.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Option   Weight   Battery   RAM / SSD   Screen notes   Price   Verdict
A       1.24 kg       15 hr     16 GB / 512 GB   13.6" and no screen drawback mentioned     $1,299       Best overall
D     1.41 kg   13 hr   16 GB / 512 GB   14" but dimmer than others   $1,219   Best value if indoor use
B     1.58 kg   9 hr     32 GB / 1 TB     14" with no display issue mentioned   $1,379   Power-first trade-off
C     1.72 kg   11 hr   16 GB / 512 GB   15.6" likely roomy for reading   $1,149   Not recommended for your stated priorities
Why A Comes Out on Top
Option   A   best matches your priorities in the order you gave them:
-   Battery life:   15 hours is the strongest here.
-   Portability:   at   1.24 kg  , it is easily the lightest.
-   RAM requirement:   16 GB meets your minimum and is enough for R, Python, Zoom, browser tabs, and light photo editing.
-   Reading comfort:   while 13.6" is smaller than 14" or 15.6", there is no note about it being dim, and the strong portability/battery advantage outweighs the size trade-off.
For a statistics grad student, this is the most balanced “carry everywhere, use all day” option.
Option 1:   A — Best overall pick     Best mix of battery life, low weight, and enough memory for your workload     Top balance
Choose A
How the Other Options Stack Up
Option 2:   D — Best budget-conscious alternative     Very good battery and still portable, but the dimmer screen is a real drawback for long reading sessions     Best value
Consider D

Option 3:   B — Best for heavier multitasking     32 GB RAM and 1 TB SSD are excellent for large datasets and longer-term headroom, but shorter battery makes it less ideal for campus mobility     Power trade-off
Compare B
Option 4:   C — Lowest rank for your needs     The larger display may help readability, but it fails your portability target at 1.72 kg     Too heavy
Skip C
Fit Notes for Your Actual Work
-   R and Python:   16 GB is sufficient for most graduate-level coursework, modeling, notebooks, and moderate data wrangling.
-   Zoom:   all four can handle it, but better battery matters a lot for long days.
-   Light photo editing:   16 GB remains fine unless you work with very large RAW files regularly.
-   Long reading sessions:   screen brightness and comfort matter, which is why   D drops behind A   despite its attractive price.
Final Recommendation
Choose   A  .

It is the only option that clearly excels in your two highest priorities—  battery life   and   portability  —while still meeting your RAM, storage, and budget requirements.   B   is tempting for its 32 GB RAM and 1 TB SSD, but for a statistics graduate student, the extra capacity is less valuable than the major hit to battery life.   D   is the runner-up if saving about $80 matters more than screen quality.   C   is the weakest fit because it misses your portability threshold.
